chunk_findings.detail: A fully quoted flag is still a flag in the parsed argv, but the new mask treats any token whose entire spelling is one quote pair as data and `_matches_flag` skips it. Given `git push origin main '--force'` or `git push "--force"`, posix tokenization yields the word `--force`, `_quoted_mask` returns true because the retained token is `'--force'`/`"--force"` with content equal to that word, and the force push is allowed. Shell parsing strips those quotes, so the command that actually runs is a real `git push` with the force flag — the case this change promised would stay refused. Exempting quote spelling, rather than matching flag words in the parsed argv and ignoring the flag text only when it is a substring of a larger argument, is the wrong predicate.
